q: Supplier invoices (Concrete examples of AI automation in SMEs)
r: Accounting, administration. Before: Invoices arrive by e-mail, as PDFs, sometimes by post. Someone opens them, re-types them into the accounting software, checks the amount, files the document. Typing errors surface at bank reconciliation. After: The invoice is read on arrival, checked against the purchase order, entered into your software and filed. The supplier receives an acknowledgement. You get a summary every morning. What stays human: Any invoice out of the ordinary (unexpected amount, unknown supplier) is set aside and shown to you with an explanation. You validate. Example 02
t: Concrete examples of AI automation in SMEs

q: Customer reminders (Concrete examples of AI automation in SMEs)
r: Sales, accounts receivable. Before: Unpaid invoices are tracked in a spreadsheet. Reminders go out when someone remembers, in a tone that varies with the person and the mood of the day. Some customers are never reminded. After: At day 7, 21 and 35, a reminder goes out automatically, in the tone you approved, with the right amount and the right invoice attached. The tracking table updates itself. What stays human: Important or sensitive customers are flagged before sending: you decide to call rather than write. Escalating to collections remains a human decision. Example 03
t: Concrete examples of AI automation in SMEs

q: Quotes (Concrete examples of AI automation in SMEs)
r: Sales, trades, engineering offices. Before: Every quote request takes an hour: reread the request, find the prices, lay it out, send it. Requests pile up at the end of the day and some wait several days. After: The request is read, the elements extracted, a quote is prepared from your price list and your previous quotes, in your usual template. It waits for you, ready to review. What stays human: Nothing leaves without your review. Atypical requests (unusual job, customer to negotiate with) are shown separately, with the points to watch. Example 04
